text_en: I said to myself, “Come now, I will make a test of pleasure; enjoy yourself. ” But again, this also was vanity.
text_cn: 我心下自语：“来，试一试快乐，享受一下福乐！”看，这也是空虚。

text_en: I said of laughter, “It is mad, ” and of pleasure, “What use is it? ”
text_cn: 我称欢笑为“疯狂”，我对喜乐说：“这有何用”？

text_en: I searched with my mind how to cheer my body with wine—my mind still guiding me with wisdom—and how to lay hold on folly, until I might see what was good for mortals to do under heaven during the few days of their life.
text_cn: 我遂决意喝酒以使我的肉身畅快，── 但我的心仍为智慧所引导，并决意迷于狂妄的事，直到我看清，世人在天下一生有限的岁月中所做的事，有什么好处为止。

text_en: I made great works; I built houses and planted vineyards for myself;
text_cn: 我于是扩大我的工程：为自己建造宫室，栽植葡萄园，

text_en: I made myself gardens and parks, and planted in them all kinds of fruit trees.
text_cn: 开辟园囿（yòu），在其中栽植各种果树，

text_en: I made myself pools from which to water the forest of growing trees.
text_cn: 挖掘水池，以浇灌在生长中的树木。

text_en: I bought male and female slaves, and had slaves who were born in my house; I also had great possessions of herds and flocks, more than any who had been before me in Jerusalem.
text_cn: 买了奴婢，还有在家中出世的僮仆，又有许多牛羊，多过我以前住在耶路撒冷的人。

text_en: I also gathered for myself silver and gold and the treasure of kings and of the provinces; I got singers, both men and women, and delights of the flesh, and many concubines.
text_cn: 我还聚敛了大批金银，及各王侯各省份的财宝；拥有许多歌唱的男女，无数的嫔妃，以及人间所有的享受。

text_en: So I became great and surpassed all who were before me in Jerusalem; also my wisdom remained with me.
text_cn: 我虽如此富有，超过以往住在耶路撒冷的人，但我仍没有丧失智慧。

text_en: Whatever my eyes desired I did not keep from them; I kept my heart from no pleasure, for my heart found pleasure in all my toil, and this was my reward for all my toil.
text_cn: 凡我眼所希求的，我决不加以拒绝；凡我心所愿享受的快乐，我决不加以阻止；因为我的心对我的一切劳苦工作，实在满意；其实，这也是我由劳苦工作应得的报酬。

text_en: Then I considered all that my hands had done and the toil I had spent in doing it, and again, all was vanity and a chasing after wind, and there was nothing to be gained under the sun.
text_cn: 但当我回顾我所作的一切工作，以及工作时所受的劳苦，看，一切都是空虚，都是追风；在太阳之下，毫无裨益。

text_en: So I turned to consider wisdom and madness and folly; for what can the one do who comes after the king? Only what has already been done.
text_cn: 我又回顾观察智慧、疯狂和昏愚；那继位作君王的人能做什么？只能做已做过的事。

text_en: Then I saw that wisdom excels folly as light excels darkness.
text_cn: 我看透智慧胜于昏愚，像光明胜于黑暗。

text_en: The wise have eyes in their head, but fools walk in darkness. Yet I perceived that the same fate befalls all of them.
text_cn: “智者高瞻远瞩，愚者却在黑暗中摸索。”但我也知道：二者都要遭遇同样的命运。

text_en: Then I said to myself, “What happens to the fool will happen to me also; why then have I been so very wise? ” And I said to myself that this also is vanity.
text_cn: 我心中自问：“愚人的命运，我也会遇到，为什么我要更明智？”我遂下结论说：“这也是空虚。”

text_en: For there is no enduring remembrance of the wise or of fools, seeing that in the days to come all will have been long forgotten. How can the wise die just like fools?
text_cn: 因为智者和愚者，同样不为人常久记念，早晚有一天都要被人遗忘。可惜，智者和愚者同样死去！

text_en: So I hated life, because what is done under the sun was grievous to me; for all is vanity and a chasing after wind.
text_cn: 于是我恼恨生命，因为太阳之下所发生的事，无非使我烦恼，因为全是空虚，都是追风。

text_en: I hated all my toil in which I had toiled under the sun, seeing that I must leave it to those who come after me
text_cn: 我憎恨我在太阳下所受的劳苦，因为我要将劳苦所得，留给我的后人。

text_en: —and who knows whether they will be wise or foolish? Yet they will be master of all for which I toiled and used my wisdom under the sun. This also is vanity.
text_cn: 他是智是愚，有谁知道；但他一定要主管我在太阳下，以智慧所辛苦经营的一切工作：这也是空虚。

text_en: So I turned and gave my heart up to despair concerning all the toil of my labors under the sun,
text_cn: 我回顾我在太阳下所受的一切劳苦，就灰心失望。

text_en: because sometimes one who has toiled with wisdom and knowledge and skill must leave all to be enjoyed by another who did not toil for it. This also is vanity and a great evil.
text_cn: 因为有人以智慧、学问和才干劳作得来的，却应留给那未曾劳作的人，作为产业：这也是空虚和大不幸。

text_en: What do mortals get from all the toil and strain with which they toil under the sun?
text_cn: 人在太阳下所受的一切劳苦，以及痛心的事，究竟有什么裨益？

text_en: For all their days are full of pain, and their work is a vexation; even at night their minds do not rest. This also is vanity.
text_cn: 其实，人天天所有的事务，无非是悲苦和烦恼；而且夜里，心也得不到安息：这也是空虚。

text_en: There is nothing better for mortals than to eat and drink, and find enjoyment in their toil. This also, I saw, is from the hand of God;
text_cn: 人除了吃喝和享受自己劳作之所得以外，别无更好的事。我也看透了：这是从天主手里来的。

text_en: for apart from him who can eat or who can have enjoyment?
text_cn: 因为离了天主，谁能有吃的，谁能有所享受？

text_en: For to the one who pleases him God gives wisdom and knowledge and joy; but to the sinner he gives the work of gathering and heaping, only to give to one who pleases God. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
text_cn: 天主原把智慧、学问和欢乐，赐给他所喜爱的人。至于罪人，天主将积蓄贮藏财物的劳苦加于他身上，好将一切财物留给天主所喜爱的人：这也是空虚，也是追风。
